title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook - Comprehensive Addendum
author: Maya Patel
summary: This document consolidates Redwood Inference's on-call and incident response processes, runbook templates, postmortem guidance, on-call rotation patterns, game day playbooks, and status page/customer communication templates. It serves as an addendum to the primary playbook and contains checklists, escalation matrices, and ready-to-send message templates for SEV-class incidents.
incident_process:
Incident Severity, Objectives, and SLOs

1) Severity classification:
- SEV0 (P0): System-wide outage affecting production inference for all customers or data-loss risk. Immediate paging and executive update required.
- SEV1 (P1): Major functional degradation (large portion of requests failing, significant latency regressions). Page on-call; high customer impact.
- SEV2 (P2): Partial degradation affecting a subset of customers or lower-priority endpoints (batch jobs, embeddings). Handle during on-call window; may not require executive comms.
- SEV3 (P3): Minor issues, non-urgent bugs, or customer-reported requests with workarounds. Handled as standard tickets.

2) Objectives for all incidents:
- Restore service to SLOs or a safe degraded mode (fallback model variant, regional failover).
- Communicate clearly to internal stakeholders and customers via status page and targeted emails.
- Preserve evidence for RCA and postmortem.
- Implement mitigating measures or rollbacks and document decisions.

3) Example SLOs and alert thresholds:
- Production inference availability: 99.95% monthly; alert when 5-minute availability < 99.5%.
- 95th percentile latency (text/generate main route): target <= 200ms; alert if 95p > 800ms for 5 minutes.
- Error rate (500-level responses): alert if >1% for 10 minutes or >0.5% for 30 minutes.

4) Paging rules:
- PagerDuty integration: page primary on-call immediately for SEV0/SEV1.
- For SEV0: page Director of SRE and Product on first notification.
- Escalation: if primary does not acknowledge within 5 minutes, escalate to secondary; after 10 minutes escalate to engineering manager.

5) Initial responder actions (first 15 minutes) - checklist:
1. Acknowledge the page and create incident channel (#incident-<id>) in Slack.
2. Determine SEV and affected services (examples: inference-gateway, router-service, autoscaler, scheduler).
3. Capture customer-facing impact and estimate ETA for the first status page update.
4. Triage: run quick health checks (kubectl/ecs service checks, recent logs, autoscaler metrics).
5. If rollback or mitigation is required, apply according to the service runbook and notify stakeholders.

6) Roles and responsibilities:
- Incident Commander (IC): owns coordination, status updates, and final mitigation decisions.
- SRE/Tech Lead: leads technical diagnostics and implements fixes (restarts, scaling, kernel-level fixes).
- Communications Lead: drafts and approves public status updates and customer emails.
- Postmortem owner: authors the RCA and tracks corrective actions.
runbooks_overview:
Runbooks: structure and templates

Each critical service runbook should include: Purpose, Owners, Key commands, Health signals, Fast-path recovery steps, Detailed recovery steps, Post-incident checks, and Rollback steps. Runbooks must be concise and executable.

Common fast-path checklist:
- Validate: confirm global vs. targeted impact using health monitors and traces.
- Scope: identify affected regions, routes, and customers using request tags and logs.
- Mitigate: enable rate limiting, enable fallback model variant, route traffic to standby region, or serve cached responses.
- Recover: restart pods with drain->terminate->recreate sequence; scale GPU nodes if capacity exhausted.
- Verify: run smoke tests (sample generation < 2s, embeddings sanity checks).

Example runbook snippet (inference-gateway):
1. Purpose: recover inference gateway when 5xx rate > 1% for 10 minutes.
2. Owners: oncall-sre, infra-team.
3. Fast path commands:
- kubectl get pods -n inference | grep inference-gateway
- kubectl logs <pod> --tail 200 | grep ERROR
- kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-gateway -n inference
- kubectl scale deployment/inference-gateway --replicas=10 -n inference
4. If GPU OOM is observed on model-server, switch to fallback model variant via admin API: POST /admin/model/switch {"service":"inference-gateway","variant":"quantized-v2-fallback"}.

Note: sensitive commands and secrets (API keys, KMS operations) must be stored in restricted-runbook entries and referenced from security-and-compliance/runbooks.
postmortem_process:
Postmortem and RCA guidance

When to write a postmortem:
- All SEV0 and SEV1 incidents must have a postmortem published within 5 business days.
- SEV2 incidents require review and may need a postmortem if systemic or customer-impacting.

Required postmortem template fields:
1. Title: [SEV#] Short description - impacted services - YYYY-MM-DD.
2. Summary: one-paragraph impact description and high-level timeline.
3. Incident timeline: timestamped events with actors and decisions (UTC).
4. Root cause analysis: what failed (component/human/process), why controls failed, why detection was delayed.
5. Corrective actions: short-, medium-, long-term actions with single owners and target dates.
6. Detection and mitigation improvements: alert thresholds, dashboards, runbook changes.
7. Customer impact and comms log: links to status updates and emails.
8. Review and acceptance: peer reviewers and sign-off.

Best practices:
- Prefer causal language ("contributed to") for complex systems.
- Include concrete metrics (error rates, latency delta, request volumes).
- Assign one owner per corrective action and a realistic due date.
- Convert systemic problems into reliability initiatives in the eng-sre roadmap.
oncall_rotations:
On-call rotations and expectations

Rotation model:
- Primary on-call: 7-day rotation (Mon 08:00 UTC - Mon 08:00 UTC).
- Secondary (backup): 7-day rotation offset by one week; supports escalation and incident assistance.
- Weekend/holiday coverage: follow the same model; pre-schedule holiday coverage as needed.

Handoffs and checklists:
- Outgoing on-call publishes current incident list, active mitigations, and planned maintenance.
- Handoff checklist: update PagerDuty schedule, post handoff note in #oncall-handoffs with summary, confirm monitoring alerts link to runbooks.

Expectations and allowances:
- Primary on-call must respond to pages within 5 minutes.
- If unable to cover a scheduled rotation, arrange a swap via the on-call scheduler and notify SRE manager.
- Shadowing: new SREs shadow primary for at least two rotations and attend a runbook review before PagerDuty access.

Compensation and time-bank details are in company-handbook.
game_days:
Game days / Chaos drills

Purpose: validate runbooks, tooling, escalation, and cross-team communication under realistic failure modes.

Schedule and ownership:
- Minimum two company-wide game days per year (Q1: rolling outage simulation; Q3: capacity stress test). Eng-SRE owns planning and retros.

Game day checklist:
1. Pre-game: define hypothesis, scope, and success criteria; notify leadership and schedule window; create a temporary internal status page entry.
2. Execute: run failure injection (node termination, disk throttling, degraded network) against staging/canary fleets first.
3. Measure: collect MTTD, MTTM, and MTTR for each scenario.
4. Post-game: publish a report with lessons learned and update runbooks/dashboards.

Common scenarios:
- Full-region failure: validate smart routing and regional failover.
- Model regression: deploy noisy canary to increase error rate and validate rollback.
- Autoscaler misconfiguration: validate circuit-breakers and safe scale limits.
status_page_and_comms:
Status page and customer communications templates

Status page principles:
- Be frequent and transparent. If no ETA, state that and commit to next update time.
- Always include impact, scope, affected regions/routes, and mitigation steps.
- Link to postmortem for SEV1/SEV0 when available.

Update cadence:
- Initial update: within 15 minutes for SEV0/SEV1.
- Follow-ups: every 30 minutes until stable, then hourly until resolved.
- Resolved: final update with summary and postmortem link.

Customer comms templates:
- Initial (short) - post on status page and send to enterprise contacts:
Subject: [Redwood] Service Degradation - Impacting inference API
Body: We are currently experiencing an issue affecting the Redwood inference API. Some requests are returning errors or experiencing elevated latency. Our SRE team is actively investigating. We will post an update by <time, UTC>. For enterprise customers, a dedicated incident bridge is available on request.

- Intermediate (medium) - mitigation deployed:
Subject: [Redwood] Incident Update - Mitigation in Place
Body: We identified the likely cause as <short cause> and have deployed a mitigation that reduces customer impact. We continue to monitor and will provide another update at <time>. Contact your account manager for dedicated updates.

- Final (long) - post-restore:
Subject: [Redwood] Incident Resolved - Summary and Next Steps
Body: Summary: On <date> at <time UTC> we experienced <impact>. Root cause: <one-paragraph root cause>. Impact: <number> customers affected for <duration>. Actions taken: <short list>. Next steps: corrective actions with owners and target dates. A full postmortem will be published by <date>.

Internal comms checklist:
- Create #incident-<id> Slack channel and pin runbook links.
- Add stakeholders and post cadence updates.
- Communications Lead reviews public messages before posting.

Canonical communication templates and canned messages are stored in: confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-communications-and-status-page-templates-2026.json
